title: AnchorSteer: Self-Discovered Concept Injection for Structure-Preserving Music Editing

problem.claim: Controllable music editing must modify high-level attributes while preserving rhythmic and melodic structures.

gap.claim: Existing steering and structural adaptation methods trade off semantic responsiveness against structural preservation because of semantic-structural entanglement.

contributions.claim: AnchorSteer couples structural anchoring with self-discovered semantic steering to address the semantic-structural tradeoff.
The framework extracts interpretable, label-free concept vectors from internal representations using a self-supervised reconstruction objective without curated data.
The framework injects portable concept vectors into diffusion hidden manifolds while a structural adaptor enforces consistency, with unconditioned and conditioned variants.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on ZoME-Bench and subjective tests reportedly show that AnchorSteer outperforms steering-only and anchoring-only baselines.
The authors report significant semantic transformations with high-fidelity structural preservation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Define controllable music editing as high-level attribute modification with rhythmic and melodic structure preserved.
Identify a tradeoff between semantic editing performance and structural preservation in existing approaches.
Introduce AnchorSteer, which combines structural anchoring with self-discovered semantic steering.
Extract label-free concept vectors and inject them into diffusion hidden manifolds under structural consistency constraints.
Report benchmark and subjective-test results against steering-only and anchoring-only baselines.

source_observation.claim: The approach separates semantic steering from structural preservation by combining concept-vector injection with a structural adaptor.

interpretation.claim: Separating control signals from preservation constraints may help manage competing objectives in structured generative editing.

application.claim: This pattern could inform editing systems that must change semantic attributes while retaining temporal or compositional structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the pattern generalizes beyond music editing or across different structures.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark protocol, datasets beyond ZoME-Bench, metrics, or effect sizes.
The abstract does not describe the architecture, training details, or subjective-test design.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
